### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via bulkCreate (symbol, a method of class TursoDriver))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via bulkCreate (symbol, a method of class TursoDriver))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via bulkCreate (symbol, a method of class TursoDriver))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c272f4c24daa9ba4bb78ffff0e940febfdbc6244` — the merge of head `821e6832c0912938ddc2d11cd419e914067e058e` into base `5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c272f4c24daa9ba4bb78ffff0e940febfdbc6244 && git checkout c272f4c24daa9ba4bb78ffff0e940febfdbc6244
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4 821e6832c0912938ddc2d11cd419e914067e058e && git checkout -B drift-repro 5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4 && git merge --no-ff 821e6832c0912938ddc2d11cd419e914067e058e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5d2ce34f88a0d3440386b381bd678a25cd59f7a4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `821e6832c0912938ddc2d11cd419e914067e058e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/boolean-write-spelling-canonical.md (declaration lines), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-boolean-write-spellings.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-local-remote-boolean-write-parity.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/boolean-written-spelling-row-scope.test.ts + none (no further file in the diff; read, not reviewed, in the live tree at this head: sql-driver-crud.ts, sql-driver-bulk-operations.ts, sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts, sql-driver-rotation.ts, sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts, sql-driver-column-creation.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3)
Security-touching: yes

No card: this PR is a security-seat no-card order. Inputs were the PR body, its seven-file list, the net diff against merge base `1bf30f8b356`, the check-runs on this head, and the dev's evidence on this head. Net diff: 7 files, +678 / -6.

### ① Derived judgments

Rule under review: on SQLite-family storage a declared scalar boolean / toggle field is stored as the boolean its value spells, whatever accepted spelling the write sends; any other value is refused 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` before a statement is built, without echoing the value; the accepted text spellings come from one table shared with the local boot convergence, whose SQL stays byte-identical; no rewrite of rows already stored; Postgres and MySQL untouched.

- Accept-set, widened — RIGHT. The text `'true'` / `'false'` / `'1.0'` / `'0.0'` and the numbers `1` / `0` used to pass through as sent; they are now bound as `sqliteBooleanBinding`'s `'1'` / `'0'`. The lookup is a `Map` (SameValueZero), so `-0` reads as `0` and `NaN` reads as nothing; `'TRUE'`, `' true'`, `''` are not in it.
- Accept-set, narrowed — RIGHT, and it is the declared narrowing. Every other non-null value on a registered boolean field (other strings, other numbers, arrays, objects, dates, bigints) is refused by `unwritableBooleanError`; it used to be stored as written. `null` and `undefined` are skipped before the lookup, and a key the payload does not own is skipped by the own-property test, so a field named `constructor` or `valueOf` is not read off the prototype.
- The refusal precedes every statement — RIGHT. Read in the live tree: `create` (sql-driver-crud.ts:362), `bulkCreate` (sql-driver-bulk-operations.ts:180, every row formed before the one INSERT), `updateMany` (:300), `rotatedUpdateById` (:354), `update` (sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts:289), `upsert` (:658) each call `formatInput` before the builder issues anything; local `bulkUpdate` goes through `update`. `SqliteWasmDriver` has no `formatInput` of its own and inherits this one.
- The refusal does not echo the value — RIGHT. The message carries the field name, the object name and `valueKind(value)` (a type word); the value itself is never interpolated.
- Remote face — RIGHT. `create`, `update`, `upsert`, `updateMany` and `bulkUpdate` already formed their payload through `toRemoteWriteForms` (which is `formatInput`) before the transport call; `bulkUpdate` maps every row before the transport runs, so it was already refuse-before-write. `bulkCreate` loops `create` per row, so the added pre-pass is what makes a refused row refuse the batch. The pre-pass discards its result and `formatInput` is copy-on-write, so the rows handed to `create` are the caller's own.
- The shared table — RIGHT. The three SQL lists rendered from the table read, in table order, `'true', 'false', '1.0', '0.0'`, `'1', '0'` and `'true', '1.0'`: the same bytes as the three literals they replace. The spellings are module constants with no quote in them, never a caller's value.
- Module evaluation — RIGHT. `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` now evaluates the table at import. `sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts` imports only `sql-driver-oracle-dialect`, `sql-driver-top-level`, `date-on-instant-column` (and `sql-driver` for types), none of which reaches `sql-driver-schema-sync`, so no evaluation cycle is formed.
- Which fields the door covers — RIGHT, as bounded. The arm reads `booleanFields[object]`, filled by `registerManagedObjectMetadata` and `registerExternalObject` for scalar `boolean` / `toggle` only (a `multiple: true` one is a JSON column and is excluded at both fills). A table the driver was never told about is not covered, as with every other coercion in `formatInput`.
- Column defaults — checked, no finding. `applyDeclaredColumnDefault` hands a literal `defaultValue` to the DDL as written, but the spec's authoring gate holds a boolean field's literal default to `z.boolean()` (`valueSchemaFor`), so authored metadata cannot give the column a text default.
- Postgres / MySQL — untouched: the arm sits below `if (!this.isSqlite) return copy`.
- Public surface: `SQLITE_BOOLEAN_TEXT_SPELLINGS` and `sqliteBooleanWriteReading` are new module exports, and the module's header states `index.ts` re-exports nothing from it. No published type, schema or export changes shape.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-sql` patch and `@objectstack/driver-turso` patch, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, the `!` title, a BREAKING paragraph, the one-line fix ("send `true` or `false`...") and one ADR-0087 marker. This matches AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: nothing a metadata author can write changes (`none` takes `patch`), and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The level is right. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` changes behaviour through its `workspace:*` dependency on driver-sql and sits in the same fixed group, so it is versioned with it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag "remote `toggle` column has TEXT affinity, noted, not filed" — answered: the canonical cell there is the text `'1'` / `'0'`, which is what the door binds; the turso pin reads `text` for that column and holds `find` and `count` to one answer on it. No action owed by this PR.
- Dev flag "the engine accepts fewer text spellings than the driver" — answered: the engine is the stricter door, so nothing the engine admits is refused below it. Held by the seat as a docs follow-up.
- Dev flag "no stored row is rewritten" — matches the maintainer ruling (no legacy-data migration); the diff adds no backfill and the local convergence SQL is unchanged.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R5 — graded in the seat's private notes. None is graded must-fix for this PR.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The only new loop is the remote `bulkCreate` pre-pass, a pure in-memory check that issues no statement.
- Check-runs at my read: 20 concluded success (among them `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `PR-body guards`); none failed. Still in progress, so NOT yet a gate verdict: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/10)` to `(10/10)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`. This record judges the design; the queue still owes every one of those green on this head. The dev's local evidence (driver-sql 4438 passed, driver-turso 2593 passed, driver-sqlite-wasm 768 passed, dogfood 4093 passed with 0 failures, ablation 28/30, 28/28 and 6/6 red) is the dev's, not re-run here.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- `sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts` — holds. The arm is the single place every SQLite-family write forms its row, so one table decides both what is stored and what is refused; the refusal carries the family and status the neighbouring write refusals carry (`sql-driver-oracle-dialect.ts:202`, `sql-driver-top-level.ts:1458`). Tried against it: a prototype-named field (own-property test), `-0` and `NaN` (Map semantics), a `multiple` boolean (never registered), a second pass over an already-formed row (`'1'` reads as `'1'`, so the remote pre-pass followed by `create` is stable), and the earlier `NOW()` pass (it can only turn a string into another string the table refuses). None breaks it.
- `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` — holds. The emitted SQL is the same bytes; the change is where the literals come from.
- `turso-driver.ts` — holds. The pre-pass sits after the column-map refusal and before the first `create`; it makes the remote batch answer a refused row the way the local single INSERT does. It does not make the remote batch atomic for any other failure, and the comment does not claim it does.
- The three test files — hold against the rule. The driver-sql pin runs all six doors against a driver-created column and a retyped TEXT column, reads `typeof` raw, and checks nothing is written on refusal. The turso pin does the same on both faces through a separate client and adds the whole-batch refusal. The runtime pin holds the engine door, the driver door and a `beforeInsert` assignment to one stored form and one answer across `find`, `count`, `findOne` and REST list / get / delete.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1 (nit) — `sql-driver-boolean-write-spellings.test.ts`'s header names `SQLITE_BOOLEAN_TEXT_READINGS`; the table is `SQLITE_BOOLEAN_TEXT_SPELLINGS`.
- N2 (nit) — `ACCEPTED_BOOLEAN_TEXT_SENTENCE` and the order of the three SQL lists depend on the table's row order (true / false pairs, canonical first). A one-line comment on the table, or a pin on the three rendered lists, would hold "byte-identical" against a later reorder.
- N3 (nit) — the changeset names `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate`; the runtime pin exercises `beforeInsert` only. The update door itself is pinned at the driver on both faces.
- N4 (nit) — a `bigint` `1n` / `0n` is now refused where it used to bind as an INTEGER; the changeset's list of accepted values is exact, so this is stated behaviour, noted for completeness.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-boolean-write-canonical`
Reviewed-by: `isolated sub-agent of session_016WV4czt69hUUaG5XcgFNYL`

**VERDICT: PASS**
